outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Foundation Models & the Adaptation Challenge
outline.description: Introduce the explosion of large foundation models, discuss why training from scratch is impractical, and explain the necessity of efficient downstream adaptation.
subtopics: Rise of large foundation models and parameter explosion
Training cost vs. deployment constraints
Downstream task adaptation: objectives and constraints
Overview of existing adaptation paradigms

outline.description: Review the main families of PEFT methods—model finetuning, adapter tuning, prompt tuning, and reparameterization—and analyze their trade‑offs.
subtopics: Model weight finetuning fundamentals
Adapter modules: adding trainable blocks
Prompt tuning: learnable prefixes
Reparameterization methods: LoRA and its extensions
Comparative analysis of efficiency, stability, and generalization

outline.description: Present the mathematical concepts of orthogonal matrices, their role in preserving angles and norms, and practical ways to enforce orthogonality during training.
subtopics: Definition and key properties of orthogonal matrices
Preserving pairwise angles and spectral norms
Cayley transform and skew‑symmetric parametrization
Orthogonality constraints in neural network training

outline.description: Explain the OFT framework, its block‑diagonal variant, and the practical advantages and limitations that motivate further research.
subtopics: OFT formulation: multiplying a learnable orthogonal matrix with frozen weights
Block‑diagonal OFT for parameter efficiency
Stability, generalization, and spectral norm preservation
High parameter count and limited expressiveness of block‑diagonal OFT

outline.chapter_title: Information‑Transmission View of Orthogonal Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Recast the problem of building a dense orthogonal matrix as transmitting information through a grid‑structured graph, and derive conditions that guide sparse factorization.
subtopics: Dense matrix as a fully connected graph
Matrix factorization as sequential graph layers
Edge‑based connectivity constraints for full transmission
Orthogonality constraints and minimum free edges
Visualizing and interpreting grid‑graph structures

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Factorization: From FFT to Structured Sparse Matrices
outline.description: Introduce the butterfly structure from the Cooley‑Tukey FFT algorithm, its recursive construction, and its suitability for efficient sparse matrix multiplication.
subtopics: Cooley‑Tukey FFT and the butterfly graph
Definition of butterfly factor and recursive construction
Permutation invariance and block‑diagonal forms
Complexity: O(d log d) edges and O(d log d) parameters
Connection to classical transforms and network topologies

outline.description: Show how to impose orthogonality on butterfly components, describe the BOFT hyperparameters, and explain how BOFT subsumes previous OFT variants.
subtopics: Enforcing orthogonality in butterfly components with Cayley transform
Hyperparameters (m, b) and their impact on expressivity and efficiency
Relationship to block‑diagonal OFT and full OFT
Identity initialization strategy for BOFT
Multiplicative dropout for regularization

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Insights into BOFT (Expressivity, Spectral, Inductive Bias)
outline.description: Present theoretical guarantees about BOFT's expressivity, spectral norm preservation, bilinear similarity view, and the inductive bias imparted by the butterfly structure.
subtopics: Expressivity theorem and approximation error vs. parameter count
Spectral norm preservation and training stability
BOFT as learning bilinear similarity with orthogonal constraints
Inductive bias from butterfly structure and its effect on generalization
Balancing expressiveness with regularization for robust finetuning

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation Across Vision, Language, Diffusion Models
outline.description: Summarize the experimental protocol, baselines, and results that demonstrate BOFT’s superiority across multiple architecture families and tasks.
subtopics: Experimental setup: datasets, models, and baselines
Results on vision transformers (image classification, segmentation)
Results on large language models (NLP benchmarks)
Results on text‑to‑image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion)
Ablation studies: hyperparameter selection, dropout, factor size

outline.chapter_title: Practical Implementation, Runtime Considerations, and Future Directions
outline.description: Provide actionable guidance for implementing BOFT, discuss runtime overhead, and outline open research questions and potential improvements.
subtopics: Implementation details: libraries, matrix multiplication, memory footprint
Training runtime overhead vs. inference latency
Choosing hyperparameters in practice (m, b, dropout rates)
Potential enhancements: alternative network topologies, optimization tricks
Open problems: most efficient information‑transmission graphs, scalability
